title: Comparing the Validity of Commonly Used Risk Assessment Tools in Men With Dual Histories of IPV and Sexual Offending
abstract: Individuals with dual histories of sexual and intimate partner violence (IPV) offending represent a complex subgroup, yet little is known about how well offence-specific risk assessment tools work for them. This field validity study compared the discrimination of an IPV risk tool (Spousal Assault Risk Assessment–Version 2; SARA-V2) with two sexual offending risk tools (Static-99R and STABLE-2007, as well as their combined risk level) in 467 men in British Columbia with dual sexual-IPV offending histories. The sexual offending measures predicted sexual recidivism with small to moderate effects, IPV recidivism with small effects, and violent recidivism with small to moderate effects. SARA-V2 total scores predicted IPV and violent recidivism with small effects but failed to predict sexual recidivism. Confidence intervals for all effects overlapped, indicating the measures had comparable discrimination. The Static-99R and Static/STABLE were the most broadly relevant in incremental validity analyses, predicting all three outcomes over and above the SARA-V2, while results for the STABLE-2007 were mixed. The SARA-V2 added predictive value to the Static-99R and STABLE-2007 for IPV and violent recidivism and to the Static/STABLE for violent recidivism. Given the SARA-V2’s risk management benefits, our findings support using the Static-99R or Static/STABLE alongside the SARA-V2 for dual sexual-IPV offending subgroups.
